sentences.text: This is a suit for ejectment of the defendants from the suit schedule property ('the premises' for short) and its vacant possession; arrears of rent of Rs.48,00,000/-, GST of Rs.69,000/- and damages of Rs.22,90,000/- upto the date of suit; arrears of electricity and water consumption charges of Rs.5,883/-; future damages at Rs.6,00,000/- p.m.; for direction to pay electricity and water consumption charges; and permanent injunction to restrain them from sub letting or carrying out interior alterations, additions and structural modifications.

2. The plaintiff's case in brief is that the 1 st defendant, represented by its partners the defendants 2 to 4, which took the premises on lease for commercial purpose under the Lease Deed dated 17.12.2018 to run a restaurant has put up temporary structure therein.
The defendants are irregular in payment of rent; cheques dated 12.10.2019 and 11.11.2019 issued towards rent were dishonoured for insufficient funds.

The rent for February 2020 was paid in six installments during September 2020 and rent for March 2020 was paid in part in four installments of Rs.1,00,000/- each on 06.10.2020, 08.10.2020, 09.10.2020 and 17.10.2020.
GST of Rs.69,000/- for March 2020 is not paid.

Owing to the defendants' default in payment of electrical consumption charges, BESCOM disconnected the power supply to the premises and she has paid Rs.5,883/- towards minimum charges to avoid removal of the meter.

After receiving the legal notice dated 23.10.2020 issued in terms of clause 4(g) of the lease deed calling upon the defendants to pay the arrears within two months on 27.10.2020, only a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- was paid by NEFT on 30.10.2020.
Instead of complying with the demand made in the legal notice, the defendants belatedly issued an untenable reply on 06.01.2021.
She has also issued notice dated 16.12.2020 demanding remittance of arrears of TDS to Income Tax department.
2(a). The defendants 2 to 4 are responsible for the day to day conduct of 1st defendant's business and are jointly and severally liable for the dues with interest at 1.5%.
The defendants are trying to induct third parties into the premises and to alter the interiors, make additions and structural modifications in order to damage the property and to harass her.

The 1 st defendant's tenancy under the lease deed stood terminated for non payment of arrears of rent and defendants 2 to 4 have forfeited their tenancy rights U/s 108(l) and (q), 111(g) and (h) of the Transfer of Property Act.

Despite termination of tenancy, the defendants have failed to quit and surrender vacant possession of the premises and therefore, are liable to pay damages at Rs.12,00,000/- p.m. for unauthorized possession.
However, she is restricting the same to Rs.6,00,000/- p.m.

The defendants are bound to pay future monthly electricity and water consumption charges upto the date of delivering vacant possession and interest at 18% p.a.

Subsequently, there was an agreement between them and the 2nd defendant whereby the 2nd defendant agreed to be solely responsible for all the liabilities arising out of the Firm.
They have not received legal notice terminating the tenancy.
After tendering resignation, they have not signed any document, particularly the postal acknowledgment.

31. Dw2 admits that the rents were not paid on time from the beginning; TDS was paid after receiving the plaintiff's notice but without paying the rent and there was no electricity supply to the premises because he was not paying the BESCOM charges.
The defendants thus, have committed breach of express conditions of Ex.P3 which amount to default resulting in termination of the lease as provided U/s 111 of the Transfer of Property Act.

32. When the arrears upto September 2020 was demanded by issuing notice at Ex.P19, but the defendants paid rent for March 2020 in installments mere acceptance of Rs.2,00,000/- towards balance rent for March 2020 after issuance of Ex.P19, in my considered opinion cannot amount to waiver.

Considering that entire arrears as demanded in Ex.P19 is not paid by the defendants despite receiving the notice and they continue to be in possession of the premises, such possession cannot be held to be lawful.
Admittedly, the last rent paid was Rs.6,00,000/- p.m. and the plaintiff has confined the damages to that extent.

As such the defendants who are in unauthorized possession of the premises are liable to pay damages Rs.22,90,000/- as claimed and accordingly, the issue for consideration is answered in favour of the plaintiff.
